originStory.title: Why I Created This Guide
originStory.subtitle: From years of tool-hopping to finally finding what works
originStory.story: I spent years searching for the perfect note-taking tool. MediaWiki. TiddlyWiki. Evernote. Google Keep. Apple Notes. Notion. Each time, I'd migrate my notes, learn the new system, and eventually hit the same wall: my notes were trapped in someone else's format, my ideas stayed disconnected, and I never felt like I truly owned my knowledge. Then I discovered Obsidian. Two things changed everything: linked thinking (the ability to connect ideas across notes and watch patterns emerge) and true data ownership (plain Markdown files I control forever). This guide exists because I don't want you to spend years finding this path. I want to hand you the map.
originStory.inspirationPoint: The realization that most beginners fail not because Obsidian is hard, but because they make the same avoidable mistakes

creatorJourney.title: From Confused User to PKM Nerd
creatorJourney.subtitle: The path that led to creating the Obsidian Starter Kit
creatorJourney.story: Before getting deep into PKM, I was just like you. Overwhelmed by information, scattered across tools, and frustrated that my notes never seemed to work for me. I'm a software developer by training, which means I've always been drawn to systems and optimization. But knowledge management isn't about the fanciest system. It's about what actually works. The moment I realized that Obsidian's plain text files meant my knowledge would survive any tool, any company, any trend. That's when everything clicked. I stopped fighting my notes and started building with them.
struggles: Migrated notes between 10+ different tools over the years
Lost important ideas because they were locked in proprietary formats
Built complex systems that collapsed under their own weight
Watched connections between ideas disappear in folder hierarchies
achievements: Created the Obsidian Starter Kit used by thousands
Published hundreds of articles on knowledge management
Built a personal vault with 10,000+ interconnected notes
Helped countless beginners avoid the mistakes I made
